title: Decision support for lumbar imaging in low back pain: an umbrella review for procurement
subtitle: Umbrella review of reviews of imaging decision support
statement: A health region is about to procure electronic decision support that checks imaging orders against appropriateness criteria. In a sample of 300 lumbar MRI requests for low back pain, 34 percent had no red flag, radiculopathy or documented conservative care. Many reviews of imaging decision support exist, overlap and sometimes disagree; the procurement board needs one appraised synthesis of what such tools achieve for appropriateness, volume, patient outcomes, override and equity.
whoAffected: Adults with low back pain in primary care and emergency departments, the clinicians who order imaging, radiology services, and the procurement board.
whatHurts: Imaging without an indication leads to further tests and treatment without better outcomes, lengthens waits for patients who need MRI, and a poorly specified tool could add alerts that clinicians ignore.
currentPractice: Imaging requests are vetted by radiologists after ordering; no decision support at the point of ordering.
whyNow: The specification is due in 2027 and the board agreed to wait for the review.
constraints: Finish by March 2027; limited reviewer time; English only.
patientCenteredGoal: People with low back pain get imaging when it will change their care and are spared imaging that will not.
summary: Problem framed as an umbrella review to inform procurement of imaging decision support.
